Chapter 9: The Justice and Mercy of God—Holding Tension
When you think about justice and mercy, it's easy to see them as opposites, isn't it? But in God, they're perfectly united.
God’s justice means He deeply cares about what’s right and wrong. He stands against evil, and you can trust that, in the end, He’ll set things right. At the same time, His mercy shows up in patience, compassion, and an incredible willingness to forgive.
Picture this: someone’s been hurt—maybe betrayed by a close friend, or let down by unfairness. The ache for justice is real, but so is the need for mercy. In God, you get both. He never overlooks wrong, but He also doesn’t take pleasure in handing out punishment. His justice is always wrapped in mercy, and His mercy never ignores the truth.
Most of us don’t realize just how much we need both. Think about it—without justice, it’s hard to feel safe. But without mercy, the world can seem pretty hopeless. What’s amazing is that God brings these tensions together in a way nobody else can. He judges with honesty, but also with deep compassion.
I remember a story about someone who found it nearly impossible to forgive. The pain ran deep, and honestly, their anger made sense. But as time passed, they saw that holding onto bitterness was like living in a prison. When they began to understand God’s justice and mercy, they discovered the freedom to finally let go. Not because the wrong didn’t matter—but because they trusted God to make things right, in His way and timing.
It’s clear now: God’s justice and mercy aren’t fighting against each other. They’re two sides of the same coin, showing a love that’s both strong and gentle. That changes how we see ourselves, and how we treat the people around us. It means we can be honest about what’s broken, but also hopeful about being forgiven.
Maybe you’ve wondered if God can really be both just and merciful. Maybe it feels like one must cancel out the other. But the whole story of God is about both—about a cross where justice and mercy come together, and a resurrection that brings new life and hope.
